newsitem.title: KENYA: Rwanda says 20 people massacred by suspected Hutus.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda says 20 people massacred by suspected Hutus.

text.p: Suspected Hutu militiamen massacred 20 people including a school headmaster, his wife and children in two attacks in central Rwanda, the state Rwanda news agency said on Tuesday.
The agency, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, said suspected Interahamwe militiamen, who played a leading role in Rwanda's 1994 genocide, struck in Nyakabanda commune.

They killed the headmaster of a secondary school, his wife and children before going on a rampage and killing other people who had encouraged local residents to collaborate with security forces, it said.
It added a total of 17 people were killed at Nyakabanda commune last Saturday and a further three were slaughtered in Mushubati commune on Friday night by another gang of militiamen.

It said security forces in Gitarama prefecture were hunting the killers and recently 30 infiltrators who had fled army operations in the north and northwest of Rwanda were captured by Nyakabanda residents.
The Rwandan government says the Hutu militiamen were among more than a million Rwandan Hutu refugees who have returned to their homeland from the former Zaire and Tanzania since last year.
Human rights groups have said the government's Rwanda Patriotic Army has killed civilians in reprisal attacks and during hunts for insurgents, which have concentrated in the northwest.
An estimated 800,000 members of the Tutsi minority and Hutu moderates were slaughtered in three months of genocide across the Central African country 1994 by Hutu troops, mobs and militiamen.
